feedback:
Judged before racing. The candidate is valid. It changes only geometry.sensor_positions x-spread, from -0.04..0.04 to -0.03..0.03 at y 0.06 and sensor_size 0.012, and keeps the iteration 7 controller (kp 4.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.30, base_speed 1.3, last_direction). Iteration 7 is the best raced design at 93.70, up from 84.33 in iteration 5. Its oval steering_oscillation of 0.246 sits just under the 0.25 return threshold, so the kd 0.30 base is acceptable.

The evidence supports a geometry test over more gain tuning. max_error has stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 m on every track in iterations 0 to 7, whatever kp, ki, kd, base_speed, sensor y or sensor_size were. Iteration 6 (sensor_size 0.016) scored lower than iteration 5 and pushed oval oscillation to 0.256, so footprint widening is not the answer. The x spread is the one geometry lever not yet tried.

The main risk is that the signal is a weighted average, so a narrower spread gives a smaller change in signal per unit of lateral offset. That is roughly a lower effective steering gain, and it may let drift grow. Narrower spacing also means less tape coverage at large offsets. Do not treat the rationale's expected drop in max_error as established. Nothing has been measured for this candidate.

After the race, decide from the telemetry. If the score is at or above 93.70 and oval steering_oscillation is under 0.25, keep x at -0.03..0.03 as the new base. If the score falls below 93.70 or oscillation exceeds 0.25, return x to -0.04..0.04 (iteration 7 geometry). If max_error is unchanged at 0.061 to 0.065 m, the next test is a wider spread (for example x -0.06..0.06) rather than more gain changes. Do not raise base_speed until progress nears 0.995 with no line loss. Completion within 3 s is not expected at base_speed 1.3.
requested_changes: If the score falls below 93.70 (iteration 7) or oval steering_oscillation exceeds 0.25, return geometry.sensor_positions x to -0.04, -0.02, 0.0, 0.02, 0.04 at y 0.06. Iteration 6 showed a wider footprint raised oscillation to 0.256, so the current sensor layout is the fallback.

If max_error stays at 0.061 to 0.065 m with line_loss_events of 1 or more and the score does not improve, test a wider x spread, for example x -0.06..0.06 (spacing 0.03 m) at sensor_size 0.012. Gain changes in iterations 2 to 4 and the footprint change in iteration 6 did not move max_error, and a narrower spread may reduce effective steering sensitivity.
Do not raise controller.base_speed above 1.3 until progress nears 0.995 with no line loss. Every run so far has gone off track, and speed only matters once the robot stays on the line.
